title: Geo-tiered failback policy for dedicated-to-hosted routing
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Context:
We need a deterministic, observable, and safe failback/failover policy that governs routing decisions when requests prefer Dedicated capacity but capacity is constrained and hosted spillover is allowed. The goal is to balance region affinity (latency + data locality), customer tier guarantees (premium vs standard), and model-quality preservation when falling back to hosted model variants. This ticket defines behavior, guardrails, telemetry, and an ops runbook for the first rollout across EU/US regions.

Problem statement:
- Customers pin routes to Dedicated pools in a region. When Dedicated pool is saturated or degraded, some requests may spill to Hosted. Uncontrolled spillover can cause silent quality regressions (different model variants), cross-region data transfer, and SLA violations for premium tiers.

Objectives:
1) Define geo-aware selection order for spillover that respects region affinity unless it violates latency SLO beyond a configurable margin.
2) Enforce tiered routing priority: premium customers should never be routed to lower-quality hosted variants without an explicit opt-in or compensating action (e.g., billing credit, alert).
3) Implement a model-variant compatibility matrix and deterministic fallback algorithm (order deterministic across controller restarts).
4) Add circuit-breakers and transient-failure backoff to avoid cascading spillovers during regional incidents.
5) Emit rich telemetry and Console signals (per-route spillover rate, quality-delta estimates, cross-region egress bytes).

Proposed design (summary):
- Routing decision inputs: {route_config, customer_tier, preferred_region, observed_latency_ms, dedicated_pool_status, model_variant_quality_scores, cost_weight}. These are normalized into a small vector and scored.
- Scoring and ordering: compute a composite score = w_region*region_penalty + w_latency*latency_penalty + w_quality*model_quality_penalty + w_cost*cost_penalty + tier_override. Lower score = preferred. Weights are configurable per-customer and per-org policy.
- Deterministic fallback order: precompute an ordered list of candidate endpoints (Dedicated same-region, Dedicated same-region-burst, Dedicated other-region (if allowed), Hosted same-region-variant, Hosted fallback-variant-1, Hosted fallback-variant-2). This list is stored versioned in route config so controllers pick the same order.
- Model variant compatibility: adopt a minimal compatibility taxonomy: exact, compatible (minor tokenization/format differences), best-effort (we expect possible quality regressions). Only routes with 'allow_best_effort' flag may use best-effort variants for premium tiers.
- Tier routing guardrail: premium routes have a max_allowed_quality_delta (default 3% A/B score drop) and max_cross_region_latency_increase_ms (default 40ms). If a candidate endpoint violates these, skip it and escalate to on-call or trigger configured compensations.
- Circuit-breakers: per-pool and per-region counters with exponential backoff. If spillover rate > 20% for 5m, open circuit for new requests for 1m and prioritize other recovery actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- A deterministic algorithm implemented in routing controller with config flags in Console.
- Unit tests for variant ordering and tier override behaviors and model-compatibility checks.
- Integration test harness that simulates dedicated saturation, cross-region penalties, and verifies chosen fallback matches expected ordering.
- Telemetry emitted: route.spillover.count, route.spillover.by_variant, route.spillover.quality_delta_estimate, route.spillover.egress_bytes.
- Ops runbook in Confluence with steps for investigating elevated spillover and for toggling spillover policies per-customer.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Strict enforcement (block requests) vs graceful degradation (serve hosted variant with alerts). Blocking preserves quality but increases error rate; graceful degradation maintains availability but risks customer dissatisfaction. Proposal: block for premium by default; allow graceful degradation if customer opts-in.
- Quality delta estimation: we can use offline evals (preferred) or a lightweight online estimator (fast but noisier). Initial release uses conservative offline-derived deltas per model pair.
- Cross-region egress cost accounting: whether to bill customers for egress when we route outside the pinned region. Currently propose to surface costs in Console and require opt-in for auto-cross-region spillover for standard tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Routing controller exposes deterministic candidate ordering and respects route.versioned_candidates
Tiered guardrails prevent premium routes from using best-effort hosted variants unless explicit opt-in
Circuit-breaker opens for high sustained spillover and prevents cascading fallthroughs
Telemetry emitted and visible in Console: spillover counts, by-variant breakdown, quality-delta estimates, cross-region egress
Integration tests validate behavior under dedicated saturation, multi-region latency penalties, and model-variant availability
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary (5% of internal test customer traffic) in us-west-2/us-east-1/eu-west-1; Phase 2: opt-in release to standard customers with Console toggle; Phase 3: default-on for enterprise/premium with monitoring alerts and on-call runbooks. Each phase gated by integration test pass and canary metrics (spillover rate < 5% and no >3% regression in quality evaluations).
